chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and from Al-Sabati, and from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that they asked both of them:

about buying the land of the Dehqans (landed gentry/farmers) from the land of the Jizya (taxation lands). So he said: 'If that is the case, it will be snatched away from you, or you will pay from it whatever is upon it in terms of land tax.'
Ammar said, 'Then he faced me and said: Buy it, for you have from the right (entitlement/value) that is more than that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on buying agricultural land subject to Jizya tax from non-Muslim or tax-paying landowners?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi addresses the permissibility of purchasing agricultural land from the Dehqans (landed gentry) in lands subject to Jizya, a key issue in Shia jurisprudence regarding property rights under Islamic governance. The Imams clarify that the buyer assumes the obligation of paying the Kharaj (land tax), while also offering eschatological hope that the land may be reclaimed by the Qaim (the Twelfth Imam) or that the spiritual and material benefits outweigh the cost. Ammar ibn Musa’s encouragement highlights the practical wisdom of securing productive assets for the community, reflecting the dynamic legal reasoning of the Ahl al-Bayt in economic transactions.
